Stage 1: Shot Volume, Shot Quality, and Big Chances

Results come from the pipeline (targets::tar_make() in the project root); this report only reads and displays them. See README.md for the reasoning behind each choice.

library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
matches <- tar_read(matches)
shots_all <- tar_read(shots_all)
shots <- tar_read(shots)
team_match <- tar_read(team_match)
stage1 <- tar_read(stage1)

1. Data

cat(sprintf("Matches: %d | All shots: %d | Open-play shots: %d\n",
            nrow(matches), nrow(shots_all), nrow(shots)))
## Matches: 1517 | All shots: 37888 | Open-play shots: 35732
show_table(as.data.frame(table(League = matches$league), responseName = "Matches"))
League Matches
La Liga 380
Ligue 1 377
Premier League 380
Serie A 380

2. Why only open-play shots

StatsBomb’s xG is calibrated for open-play shots but underrates direct set-piece shots, so those are excluded (penalties were excluded in the Understat work too).

show_table(xg_calibration_by_type(shots_all))
set_piece n goals expected ratio z
Open Play 35732 3453 3363.9 1.03 1.5
Free Kick 1749 113 69.5 1.63 5.2
Penalty 400 300 313.4 0.96 -0.8
Corner 7 3 0.0 2380.95 84.5

5. Why volume and quality are modelled separately

If team xG followed a single Tweedie distribution, these five estimates of its index would agree.

plot_p_compare(stage1)

show_table(p_compare_table(stage1))
Estimate p 95% interval Gap from fitted p (in fitted-p SEs)
Tweedie fit 1.487 1.328 to 1.645 0.0
Volume elasticity (2 - e) 1.394 1.354 to 1.433 -1.1
Quality elasticity (1 + e) 1.392 1.345 to 1.439 -1.2
Shot shape (moments) 1.635 - 1.8
Shot shape (MLE) 1.494 - 0.1

What each component is, and whether StatsBomb’s xG is calibrated within it. The top component defines a big chance.

show_table(component_profile(shots))
component n share median_xg median_distance pct_header pct_first_time goal_rate goals_over_xg
1 1713 0.048 0.0070 34.5 0.004 0.159 0.009 1.33
2 30400 0.851 0.0475 19.3 0.182 0.318 0.063 1.01
3 3619 0.101 0.3500 8.9 0.156 0.528 0.416 1.04

The mixture refit within each league and within two random halves of the matches. Leagues should reproduce the pooled structure; halves can disagree because smaller samples cannot always separate it, which is why the mixture is fit once on the pooled data.
